title: Quran Study 69: Fasting, the Revelation of the Quran, Dawn Prayer, and Answered Prayer (1982-12-17)
date_note: Explicit in the filename. The recording ends during a personal accident story.
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/69 - Friday Sermon 17 Dec. 1982 By Dr. Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A Sura 2 study beginning with Quran 2:183–186. Fasting is traced to Abraham and the lunar month of Ramadan. Rashad discusses illness, travel, feeding a poor person, pregnancy, long summer days, and the claim that fasting is best whenever physically possible. Quran 2:185 leads into a detailed theory that the whole Quran was placed into Muhammad's heart on one Night of Power at the highest Masjid al-Aqsa and then released by Gabriel in small portions over twenty-three years. The group discusses the early revelation sequence, nineteen-word and nineteen-letter structures, the spelling Becca, preservation, Muhammad's altered state during revelation, memorization, scribes, verse placement, Sura titles, qiblah instructions, and the marriage to Zayd's former wife. The study returns to fasting as a designed test, Dawn Prayer, the body as a wild horse, gradual progress in the five prayers, charity toward poor and transient people, Quran 2:186, God's nearness, and the timing of answered prayer. The file ends while Rashad recounts a traffic accident in Tripoli that he interpreted as correcting his belief that prayers require three to six months to be answered.

sections.title: Quran 2:183–184, fasting through Abraham, Ramadan, illness, travel, feeding the poor, and fasting as best
sections.summary: Rashad says fasting existed before Muhammad and came through Abraham. The specified days are the lunar month of Ramadan. Illness and travel permit postponement, serious difficulty permits feeding a poor person, and voluntary extra feeding is praised, but the verse's ending is used to say fasting remains best whenever possible.

sections.title: Duties, charity toward transients, Quran 2:186, God's nearness, answered prayer, angels, and the Tripoli accident
sections.summary: Rashad lists prayer, zakat, Ramadan fasting, Hajj, charity, and kindness as duties and criticizes hostility toward poor and transient people. Quran 2:186 says God is near and responds to callers who respond to Him and believe. He says a believer's prayer is always answered at the best time and that angels may act quickly on spoken wishes without knowing inner thoughts. The recording ends during a story in which he concluded prayer took three to six months, then struck a child with a car in Tripoli and interpreted the event as immediate correction.
